title: Unbounded limit and unstable sort — pagination that silently loses rows
expected_feedback: Standard (S4, nature [D], trigger T5 live): two defects. (1) No server-side maximum on `limit` — one partner can request 100k rows and take the service down; cap it (100 is a common default) and document the cap. (2) The sort key is not unique, so rows sharing a created_at value have no deterministic order between requests: an item can appear on two consecutive pages or on neither. Append a unique tie-breaker such as `id` to every sort. At 40M rows with a high insert rate, offset pagination also drifts as rows are inserted ahead of the cursor position — recommend cursor pagination for this dataset. Because the callers are untrusted (T5), the unbounded limit is a FAIL rather than a WARN.
